**Qwen3 14B→32B** has the highest BoolQ retention among the held-out benchmarks, at **101.9%** (Table 18, p. 21).

A value above 100% means the mapped-KV transfer scored slightly higher on BoolQ than the 32B target's own standalone accuracy. Retention is defined as transfer accuracy divided by target standalone accuracy on the same benchmark (p. 21; definition also on p. 6).

The next highest are Qwen3 8B→32B at 99.9% and Llama 3.1 8B→70B at 96.2% (p. 21).

The selected k values are fixed for this evaluation. The paper says "Neither the fit nor k is changed, so this measures the reported configuration out of sample" (p. 21). BoolQ is one of the three held-out benchmarks never used to select k, along with PIQA and ARC-Easy (p. 21).
